The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'hover_custom_background' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. wp_kses_post applied to post content on save does not parse shortcode attribute text, allowing injected double-quotes to survive storage and break out of the style attribute context at render time.

The PublishPress Tag Groups: Stylish Displays For Your Tags and Categories plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'separator' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is possible because wp_kses_post applied on save treats HTML-entity-encoded payloads as inert text, but the plugin's own check_attributes() function calls html_entity_decode() on the separator value before passing it to unescaped output, reconstituting live markup at render time.

The PublishPress Tag Groups: Stylish Displays For Your Tags and Categories plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'column_gap' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload bypasses wp_kses_post sanitization on save because it contains no HTML tags — only a double-quote character within shortcode attribute syntax that breaks out of the style attribute at render time.

The Fastcache by Host.it plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 's' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.14 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. This code path is only reachable when both the Light Images feature and the DOMDocument entity-decode branch are enabled (lightimgs_status = 1 and img_processing_entity_decode = 1), which reflect the default plugin configuration.

The Coupon Creator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is only exploitable when an administrator has enabled the 'Disable Print View' option (cctor_hide_print_link), as this setting is required to reach the vulnerable else branch; the default configuration is not affected.

The Booking Calendar plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the plugin's 'booking' shortcode in all versions up to, and including, 12.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on user supplied attributes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not keep a subscriber's secret key out of the redirect it returns after a subscription request when double opt-in is enabled, allowing unauthenticated attackers to confirm a subscription for any email address without access to its mailbox and, when the address already has an unconfirmed subscription, to reset that record with their own details.

The RSVPMaker for Toastmasters WordPress plugin before 6.9.3 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before outputting it back in an admin page, leading to a Reflected Cross-Site Scripting which could be used against high privilege users such as admin.

The Titan Anti-spam & Security  WordPress plugin before 7.5.5 does not protect or remove the diagnostic archive it writes to the uploads folder when an administrator exports its logs, and names it after the export date alone, allowing unauthenticated visitors to download the Titan Anti-spam & Security  WordPress plugin before 7.5.5's logs, including visitor IP addresses, and the site's system information.

The Keywords to Links Converter WordPress plugin before 2.2.5 does not validate a value submitted to one of its AJAX actions before saving it as an option that it later uses in an arithmetic operation on every admin and front-end request, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to make the whole site return a fatal error until the option is manually reset.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.8.0 does not check that a lesson belongs to the course a course creator is authorised to manage before moving it, allowing a user with the Course Creator role to move lessons out of other creators' courses into their own and read their content.

The Keywords to Links Converter WordPress plugin before 2.2.5 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement via an AJAX action available to any authenticated user, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to perform SQL injection attacks and read arbitrary data from the database.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not verify that a referenced media item belongs to the user, or is not already attached elsewhere, before re-linking it to their own content, and its media identifiers are predictable from public post data, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to take over and delete media uploaded by other users, including administrators.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.7.0 does not verify that the user is allowed to manage the space it actually modifies or deletes, allowing a user who administers any one space to modify or permanently delete any other space on the site, together with its posts, comments, reactions and memberships.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not apply the per-link visibility rules of space sidebar links when listing spaces in its space discovery feature, allowing unauthenticated visitors to retrieve the titles and URLs of links restricted to logged-in users or specific memberships, as well as disabled links, for every public and private space.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict the content type of its lightbox shortcode, allowing users with the contributor role and above to make the lightbox fetch HTML from an attacker-controlled server and insert it into the page unsanitised, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting when a user opens the lightbox.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict which PHP functions a shortcode's filter attribute can call, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to remove WordPress' term-slug sanitization and perform SQL injection attacks through another shortcode's taxonomy term attribute.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not escape the error message returned when a remote feed cannot be retrieved before outputting it, which could allow users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators by pointing the feed at a server they control.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent placeholders in a shortcode attribute from being expanded with unescaped nested shortcode output, allowing users with a role as low as contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent format specifiers in a shortcode attribute from being interpreted when building navigation menu markup, which could allow users with a role as low as Contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

The Payment forms, Buy now buttons, and Invoicing System | GetPaid WordPress plugin before 2.8.63 does not check that the visitor is allowed to view an invoice before rendering it through its single-invoice shortcode, and its payment-form embed page lets unauthenticated users render that shortcode for any invoice ID, disclosing customers' names, billing addresses, phone numbers, line items and payment status.

The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not protect its unsubscription actions against Cross-Site Request Forgery for subscribers it identifies from its own tracking cookie, allowing attackers to unsubscribe a subscriber from the site's newsletter by making them visit a malicious page.

The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not properly validate the destination of the redirect performed when a subscriber changes their list membership from a newsletter link, checking only that it begins with the site's URL, allowing unauthenticated attackers to redirect users to external sites whose address starts with the site's URL.

The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not check that a visitor is really the subscriber before showing them newsletters marked as private, and accepts a weaker subscriber identifier that anyone can obtain by submitting a known subscriber's email address to the public subscription form, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a subscriber's email address to read every private newsletter sent to that subscriber.

The RSVP and Event Management WordPress plugin before 2.7.19 does not escape a submitted value before outputting it back in its RSVP form when the form is re-displayed after a failed submission, leading to a Reflected Cross-Site Scripting which could be used against high-privilege users such as admins.

The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 does not limit one of its HTML output rewriting patterns to the markup it targets, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject HTML attributes through a comment author name that execute as Stored XSS for any visitor, including logged-in administrators, on pages that list recent comments.

The Coupon Creator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (with metakeyinput=cctor_expiration)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is possible because the cctor_coupon post type advertises 'custom-fields' support, enabling WordPress core's Custom Fields metabox for Contributors, and the unregistered cctor_expiration meta key causes sanitize_meta() to be a no-op, allowing raw HTML to be stored verbatim in the database via a single AJAX request.

The ProfilePress  WordPress plugin before 4.18.1 takes the role for an account registered through a combined login and registration form from the separate registration form that shares its numeric ID, allowing unauthenticated users to register with the elevated role, such as Editor, assigned by an unpublished registration form.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve the escaping of JSON-formatted database values when they rewrite the database during a restore to a new address or server, which could allow unauthenticated attackers to plant harmless-looking escaped markup, for example in a comment author name, that becomes Stored Cross-Site Scripting once an administrator performs such a restore.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep serialized string lengths consistent when their database search and replace processes certain serialized values, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data that becomes an attacker-chosen PHP object after an administrator runs a URL-lengthening search and replace or a migration restore.

When the replacement changes the length of the text, the declared string lengths inside the stored value no longer match and the corrupted value is written back, so when WordPress later reads it the trailing bytes are parsed as further serialized structure, including an object of a class the attacker named. No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on classes available from other installed code.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep a serialized value inert when their database search and replace reaches its recursion limit, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data in their own user meta that is rewritten into a live PHP object when an administrator later runs a search and replace or a migration restore, and is then instantiated by WordPress on a later read.

This is distinct from CVE-2024-10957, whose fix restricted the unserialize call but left this path in place. No gadget chain is present in WordPress core or the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on a suitable class from another installed UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or .

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not safely process the output of the external database dump tool when backing up large tables, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to store profile data that turns into SQL executed when an administrator later restores the backup, for example to grant themselves the administrator role.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve long database values byte-for-byte when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a serialized value that becomes a PHP Object Injection once an administrator backs up and restores the database.

No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or WordPress core, so the demonstrated effect is instantiation of an attacker-chosen class in the attacker's own requests. Exploitation requires the planted data to line up exactly with how the backup is read back, which depends on details of the attacker's row and the database dump format.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not correctly handle comment-like content found in the middle of a long SQL statement when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber who have stored crafted content in their own profile to have SQL executed when an administrator later restores a backup, and so escalate their account to administrator.

This is a different code path from the backup restore issue fixed in 1.26.10, and it does not depend on the database server's maximum packet size.

The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This is due to the plugin splicing the attacker-controlled request URI into a PHP expression inside a double-quoted string and evaluating it with eval(). Because PHP interpolates double-quoted strings, a payload of the form {${...}} in the URL path is executed during interpolation, so no quote breakout is required and WordPress' slashing does not mitigate it. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server with a single GET request. The affected conditions ship enabled by default and are evaluated before any logged-in check, so no plugin configuration is needed; the site must have BuddyPress and Paid Memberships Pro active alongside this plugin.

The Salon Booking System – Appointment Booking for Salons, Barbershops & Spas plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 10.31.16. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite arbitrary users' user meta fields, including the _sln_phone and _sln_sms_prefix meta of administrator accounts, and create bookings attributed to arbitrary users. This is exploitable on default installations because reCAPTCHA is disabled by default, causing the booking endpoint's permission check to return true for any authenticated user without a meaningful authorization gate.

The Mapster WP Maps — Mapbox, MapLibre & Google Maps for WordPress plugin before 2.0.7 does not perform any authorization check when saving edits made through its bundled photo-gallery library, allowing any authenticated user with at least Contributor-level access to overwrite the title and content of, and write arbitrary metadata onto, any post, page or media attachment on the site regardless of ownership.

The GiveWP  WordPress plugin before 4.19.2.1 does not properly restrict access to sensitive donor information in one of its REST API endpoints, allowing any authenticated user who owns a donor record, such as a subscriber who has donated once, to retrieve the email address, phone number, name, postal address and company of all donors.

The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check that a requested Zoom meeting's recordings were published on the site before fetching them with the site's connected Zoom account, allowing unauthenticated users who know a meeting ID to retrieve that meeting's cloud recording details, including its topic, share link, passcode when returned by Zoom, and direct play and download links.

The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check authorization, or whether a meeting is restricted to logged-in users, password-protected or unpublished, before returning a meeting's join links, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain the passcode-embedded join links of any meeting, including meetings the site restricts.

The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check that the requester is authorized to join a meeting before issuing a Zoom Meeting SDK signature for it, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain a valid signed join credential for an arbitrary meeting.

The GiveWP  WordPress plugin before 4.19.2.1 does not exclude donors who chose to give anonymously from one of its public REST API listings, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve those donors' names.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.10, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.10.26 does not guard all execution paths of its database restore process against second-order SQL injection, allowing a Subscriber-level user who has stored crafted content in their own account to escalate to administrator when an administrator later restores a backup.
This is due to an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-108761 in 1.26.9: the fix guards only one of the restore routine's execution paths, and a second path remains exploitable.

A flaw was found in Quay. Insufficient validation of repository notification webhook URLs allows an authenticated administrator to trigger Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). By specifying an internal URL or a redirect to an internal destination, an attacker can force the Quay worker to issue unauthorized HTTP requests to internal network locations and cloud metadata services.

The WP Import Export Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Limited Code Injection in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.32 via the 'comment' parameter. This is due to a two-stage shortcode check that evaluates the raw mapping placeholder before data substitution, causing the neutralizer to be skipped when attacker-controlled comment content containing a malicious [wpie_function] shortcode is substituted at runtime. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP callables on the server. Exploitation requires an Administrator to perform the standard Export With Settings For Import followed by a New Import migration workflow, which is a routine operational task; the attacker themselves requires no account or authentication, needing only the ability to submit a pending comment on any comments-open post.

The rtMedia for WordPress, BuddyPress and bbPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'media_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.7.18 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The vulnerability is only triggerable via the Backbone.js-rendered "Load More" pagination path; the server-side PHP gallery rendering correctly escapes media_title with esc_attr() and is not affected.

Observable Discrepancy vulnerability in Drupal CAPTCHA for Drupal 7 allows unauthenticated attackers to test login credentials despite CAPTCHA protection.

When CAPTCHA is enabled on Drupal login forms, normal form validation can still run after a missing or incorrect CAPTCHA response. This may expose credential validation feedback and allow an attacker to distinguish invalid credentials from valid credentials paired with a failed CAPTCHA.



This issue affects CAPTCHA for Drupal 7: from 7.x-1.0 through 7.x-1.7.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Icon API: Menu submodule of the Drupal 7 Icon API module. When a menu item is configured with the Title Wrapper option enabled, the value of the Title Wrapper Class field is output directly into an HTML attribute without sanitization or escaping. A user with the "administer menu icons" permission can inject a payload such as `title" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)` that is rendered verbatim on every page displaying the affected menu item, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any user who interacts with the menu link. This can lead to session theft, account hijacking, and further attacks against site users.

This issue affects Icon API 7.1.0.

audio-separator before 0.47.2 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying malicious Demucs .th model files loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False. Local users writing to the shared /tmp/audio-separator-models/ default directory, or attackers controlling unverified model download sources, can execute code when victims run Demucs separation.

Cesanta Mongoose 7.21 before 7.24 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in rx_ip6() checksum validation that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read past received packets by sending IPv6 extension headers. Attackers can send a single IPv6 TCP or ICMPv6 packet with extension headers, causing tcp6csum_ok() and icmp6csum_ok() to use the full payload length and read adjacent receive-buffer memory.

Cesanta Mongoose 7.22 before 7.24 with the built-in TLS stack contains an out-of-bounds read in mg_timegm() that allows remote attackers to crash the process via crafted X.509 certificate validity months. Attackers can present a certificate with month '00' or out-of-range values during the handshake, before signature verification, causing an unchecked dm array index and denial of service.

Qwik City before 1.20.3 (@builder.io/qwik-city) and @qwik.dev/router before 2.0.0-rc.4 contain an improperly controlled object modification vulnerability in formToObj that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite built-in function properties. Attackers can send a form POST with nested field names traversing inherited members of string values, breaking Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call process-wide until server restart.

devpi-server before 6.21.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write files outside the +files storage root by naming a user and index '..'. Attackers can self-register a '..' user, create a '..' index, and upload release files with attacker-chosen filenames and contents into a parent of the server directory.

devpi-web before 5.2.0 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the +doc documentation route because docs_file_exists and docs_file_path in doczip.py never confine relpath to the documentation directory. Attackers can request a relpath with a leading // or percent-encoded .. segments to read server files, including the keyfs sqlite database holding password hashes.

probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an unbounded memory buffering vulnerability in parseExif in lib/parse_stream/webp.js that allows remote attackers to exhaust memory via an attacker-declared EXIF chunk length. Attackers can supply a WebP stream or URL to probe(url) or probe(stream) declaring a huge EXIF length after VP8X, causing unbounded buffering and process memory exhaustion.

probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in lib/parse_stream/avif.js that allows remote attackers to exhaust memory via attacker-declared ftyp or meta box sizes. Attackers can supply an AVIF stream or URL to probe(url) or probe(stream) declaring a huge box length, forcing the parser to buffer all received bytes and causing denial of service.

probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an algorithmic-complexity denial of service vulnerability in lib/exif_utils.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying self-referencing EXIF IFDs. Attackers can submit a crafted 9.6 KB JPEG with repeated ExifIFD and InteropIFD pointers to block the Node.js event loop for about 23 seconds.

probe-image-size 7.4.0 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in lib/common/svg_header.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to block the event loop via crafted SVG doctypes. Attackers can supply SVGs with an unclosed internal subset followed by many ']' characters to trigger quadratic backtracking in probe.sync, probe(stream) or probe(url), causing repeated event loop stalls.
